method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach' (published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9)), 28 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13558519). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408) 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents' (published 10 November 2020), 15 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC7984068). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the PeDRA retinoid consensus (Europe PMC JATS XML through pmc_text.py; its 15 recommendation tables were stripped, so claims come from the narrative), paraphrased under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; the S1 claims are unchanged. Source text: the article abstract (tags stripped) followed by the body text from pmc_text.py, both from the Europe PMC JATS XML. The 68 consensus recommendations are in tables and supplementary tables, which were stripped; the claims come from the abstract and narrative. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Tables 2-4 (differential diagnosis, clinical assessment, treatment) and S2 Tables 2, 5 and 8 (retinoid-responsive subtypes, giving capsules to children, bone monitoring) are paraphrased from the row lines. S1 Table 1 (the summary) and S2 Tables 3, 4, 6, 7 and 9-14 were not extracted (ragged rows or merged cells).

claims.claim: **Darier disease is a rare autosomal dominant genodermatosis** from ATP2A2 variants (the SERCA2 calcium pump). It usually starts after puberty, with triggers and variable severity.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Typical signs:** symmetrical crusted keratotic papules in seborrhoeic areas, which can merge into thick, fissured, smelly plaques in the folds; palmar pits, wart-like papules on the hands and feet, and nail changes.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnosis is mainly clinical,** backed by family history, histology or cytology and, where possible, ATP2A2 testing. Offer genetic counselling to the patient and relatives at risk.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Flares follow heat, sweating, friction, UV, stress, hormonal change, surgery, infection or vaccination,** and drugs such as lithium, oral contraceptives, calcium-channel blockers, azathioprine and interferon.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Late or sudden onset should prompt a search for a paraneoplastic cause, HIV infection, recent major surgery or immunosuppression.** Early clues are nail changes and wart-like papules on the backs of the hands and feet. Examine the whole skin with the mouth, eyes and genitals, and the nails for red or white longitudinal bands, a V-shaped notch at the free edge and subungual hyperkeratosis.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The main differential is Hailey–Hailey disease:** painful, malodorous, erosive lesions in the folds, white nail bands in more than 70% but no red lines or fragile nails, earlier onset and less itch; histology separates the two. Others are acrokeratosis verruciformis of Hopf (an allelic ATP2A2 disorder on the backs of the hands and feet) and Grover disease, a transient acquired eruption mostly of middle-aged and older men.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For suspected mosaic disease, sequence ATP2A2 in both lesional skin and blood.** A negative test does not exclude Darier disease: unusual variants can be missed, and some mild, atypical, sporadic or mosaic cases never reach a molecular diagnosis.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspect secondary infection** (Staphylococcus aureus, Candida, HSV and others) when lesions worsen fast, stop responding, become painful, or show vesiculopustules, confluent erosions or white exudate, or with fever, malaise or nodes.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Disseminated infection can become Kaposi varicelliform eruption, erythroderma or sepsis,** and occasionally fatal multi-organ failure.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keratinocyte cancers (squamous and basal cell) arise more often on Darier lesions,** so check persistent or changing lesions.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **When infection is suspected, take swabs, PCR or cultures and start empirical antiviral or antibacterial treatment straight away; admit Kaposi varicelliform eruption to hospital at once.** With recurrent infections, screen the patient and family members for S. aureus carriage on skin and in the nose, and always exclude active infection before immunosuppressants or systemic steroids.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First-line care is trigger avoidance, antiseptics, emollients and topical anti-inflammatories;** systemic treatment is for moderate-to-severe or refractory disease.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use octenidine or chlorhexidine antiseptics regularly** to lower colonisation and secondary infection.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat localised bacterial infection with a short course of fusidic acid 2% cream;** avoid prolonged or repeated topical antibiotics because of resistance.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Topical retinoids help:** adapalene 0.1% once daily for 2 months reduced lesions and was well tolerated. Sun protection, avoiding temperature extremes and emollients reduce early irritation.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For flares, moderate-to-potent topical corticosteroids are often needed.** Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment (then 0.03% maintenance) or pimecrolimus is preferred in skin folds.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Topical corticosteroid classes (S1's treatment table):** class II–III for temporary use, and class IV only briefly for acute flares, each matched to the body site and situation.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Oral retinoids are the first-line systemic treatment for Darier disease** and have transformed care of keratinisation disorders, but they are highly teratogenic: post-menarchal females need a strict pregnancy prevention programme.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acitretin works, but the benefit lasts only while it is taken.** Safety data from congenital ichthyosis are largely reassuring. Watch for haemorrhagic blisters on the hands and feet after minor trauma, a Darier-specific effect.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Isotretinoin:** in an open study of 104 patients about 70% improved within 1–4 weeks, but 11 stopped for side effects; long-term use in ichthyosis has been linked to bone toxicity.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alitretinoin 30 mg/day** has helped young women in whom acitretin failed or was unsuitable because of childbearing potential; relapse on dose reduction or stopping was common.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other oral options are anecdotal,** for example doxycycline 100 mg/day in two case reports, with no long-term data.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Acitretin is the preferred oral retinoid** for its efficacy and better safety, notably for bone: 0.25–0.5 mg/kg/day or less, set to the clinical situation, with liver tests, lipids and (where relevant) skeletal checks. Isotretinoin suits short courses, given doubts about its long-term bone safety; alitretinoin is the option for women who may want a pregnancy, since contraception is needed for only 1 month after it is stopped.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Before an oral retinoid, screen for self-harm and suicide risk,** particularly with a past psychiatric history, extensive disease or poor quality of life; depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, epilepsy and other neuropsychiatric conditions are looked for systematically. If the patient takes lithium, consider an alternative.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **JAK, IL-23, IL-17 and IL-4/13 inhibitors rest only on case reports and series,** with inconsistent benefit and safety; watch for skin infection if one is tried. MEK inhibitors, dantrolene and HSV-1-based gene therapy remain under investigation.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The ichthyoses and related disorders of cornification arise from variants in more than 50 genes.** Care is built on frequent bathing, humidified air, daily emollients and keratolytics, with topical and oral retinoids as a key addition.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Topical retinoids (tazarotene, tretinoin, adapalene) lessen scale and can correct ectropion.** They carry less risk than oral retinoids and suit milder disease, but irritate, more so in ichthyosis vulgaris, atopic skin and fragile skin.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Offer a risk-benefit discussion about an oral retinoid to families of children with moderate to severe disease and real functional or psychological impact.** Genetic testing does not predict who will respond.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Aim for the lowest dose that reaches and holds the goal, usually 1 mg/kg/day or less.** Treatment is often lifelong because the skin returns to baseline when it stops; continuing topical care may allow a lower oral dose or breaks.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Isotretinoin and acitretin work about equally.** Acitretin peels palms and soles more (favouring it for palmoplantar disease) but causes more persistent hair loss; isotretinoin's short half-life eases dose changes, breaks and family planning. In Netherton syndrome, skin toxicity usually outweighs benefit.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Neonates with harlequin ichthyosis whose scale restricts breathing or endangers the limbs may benefit from an oral retinoid;** milder cases may not need one.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Subtypes where oral or topical retinoids have improved scale:** lamellar ichthyosis, epidermolytic ichthyosis, harlequin ichthyosis, some genotypes of congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma, erythrokeratodermia variabilis, ichthyosis with confetti, recessive X-linked ichthyosis, loricrin keratoderma, the KID, KLICK and IFAP syndromes, neutral lipid storage disease with ichthyosis and Sjögren–Larsson syndrome. **No data, or no benefit:** CHILD, CHIME, Conradi–Hünermann–Happle, MEDNIK and Refsum syndromes, ichthyosis prematurity syndrome, the ichthyosis–hypotrichosis syndromes (with or without sclerosing cholangitis), peeling skin disease and trichothiodystrophy.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Giving a retinoid capsule to a child:** it can be swallowed whole or chewed, pierced (the shell is tough) and squeezed onto food, softened for 2–3 minutes in a little warm milk or water, for an infant, stirred into a small amount (1 oz) of formula or breast milk, or frozen inside a small soft-centred chocolate; fatty food helps absorption. Keep capsules out of direct sunlight and use each one as soon as it is unpacked.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lipids and liver tests at baseline, again 1–2 months after starting, then every 6–12 months while normal.** Combined oral contraceptives also raise lipids; persistently high lipids can be treated while the retinoid continues if the balance of risk is acceptable.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Bone:** premature epiphyseal closure is uncommon but serious, reported above 1 mg/kg/day over 4–6 years. Check growth yearly, ask about musculoskeletal symptoms and diet, and on long-term treatment consider baseline imaging repeated after 3–5 years (sooner for symptomatic sites).
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Bone monitoring in detail (S2 Table 8):** for children, a yearly growth check (height, weight, BMI and growth curve), questions about diet (enough vitamin D, no extra vitamin A) and, once growth is complete at 16–18 years, a baseline skeletal survey (lateral cervical and thoracic spine, lateral calcanei including the Achilles tendon, hips and any painful site) with a bone density scan such as DEXA. Adults expected to stay on treatment get the same baseline survey, repeated every 3–5 years or when symptoms appear.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Eyes:** a baseline examination by an experienced ophthalmologist, lubricants or preservative-free tears during treatment, review after 4–6 months and then every 6–12 months on long-term treatment; pause or stop if retinal function worsens.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ask about mental health at baseline and at follow-up in everyone with a disorder of cornification,** whatever the treatment: depression and anxiety are common in ichthyosis itself.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid pregnancy for 3 years after stopping acitretin** (with alcohol it forms etretinate, which is stored in fat). Prefer isotretinoin for anyone of reproductive potential, and consider switching from acitretin to isotretinoin at puberty, or at least long-acting reversible contraception.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Raise contraception early with adolescents on a retinoid,** review it every visit, and agree when it will start (for example at 16 years, or before first sexual activity), with help from a gynaecologist if needed.
claims.locator: Pediatric Dermatology Research Alliance (PeDRA) Use of Retinoids in Ichthyosis Work Group (Zaenglein AL, Levy ML, Stefanko NS, et al.), Pediatric Dermatology 38(1):164-180 (doi 10.1111/pde.14408), 'Consensus recommendations for the use of retinoids in ichthyosis and other disorders of cornification in children and adolescents', published 10 November 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7984068/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ablative laser, cryotherapy and photodynamic therapy are for localised lesions that resist treatment.** Care should be multidisciplinary (neuropsychiatric, eye, dental, obstetric); lasting remission is not yet achievable, so treatment is individual.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Of the physical options, ablative CO2 or Er:YAG laser (fractional or not) has the best evidence** and can give lasting results with an experienced operator. Cryotherapy and local surgery risk pigment change, scarring and recurrence; botulinum toxin can reduce flares provoked by sweating, but only for a time.
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Let the gynaecologist know about the diagnosis:** Darier disease can give abnormal Pap smear results. In pregnancy, watch for flares and obstetric problems (skin, intrauterine or perinatal infection, traumatic delivery, difficulty breastfeeding).
claims.locator: European Reference Network for Rare and Undiagnosed Skin Disorders (ERN-Skin) expert panel, Dermatology and Therapy, 'Consensus Recommendations for Management of Darier Disease: A Practical Approach', published 15 July 2026 (vol 16, issue 9), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13558519/, retrieved 2026-09-23
